findings.title: Double-checked locking is incomplete; concurrent callers will redundantly re-read the manifest
findings.body: The function checks the cache under RLock, then re-acquires a write Lock to populate it. However, it does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write Lock. When N goroutines invoke GetWebAssets concurrently while the cache is still nil (typical at server startup), every one of them passes the RLock check, then takes the write Lock sequentially, and each independently reads `assets-manifest.json` from disk and overwrites the global. The expensive I/O — the very reason the cache exists — is repeated N times. After `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` (line 48) and before the `cdn := ""` line, add `if entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` to make this a correct double-checked locking pattern. Without it, the race detector is silenced but the cache offers no benefit under cold-cache concurrency.

findings.title: No regression test added for the data race fix
findings.body: This PR explicitly fixes a data race on `entryPointAssetsCache`, yet no test file is added or modified. There is no existing concurrent test for GetWebAssets that would have caught the original race, and nothing here guards against reintroducing the same race (e.g. by removing the mutex or by reverting to the unlocked read in a future refactor). A short test that calls GetWebAssets from many goroutines in parallel and runs under `go test -race` would lock the fix in place and exercise the double-checked locking pattern described above.

findings.title: Cache is overwritten with nil on read error, defeating caching for subsequent calls
findings.body: On line 69 the code unconditionally assigns `entryPointAssetsCache = result` and on line 70 returns `entryPointAssetsCache, err`. If `readWebAssetsFromFile` returns an error (network blip, transient I/O failure), `result` is nil and the global cache is overwritten with nil. Because the write Lock is held, every concurrent caller will observe the cleared cache and will each attempt the file read again; any previously cached value is permanently lost even if it was still valid. The assignment should only happen on success, e.g. `if err == nil { entryPointAssetsCache = result }` before the return. (Note: this behavior pre-existed, but the PR is the natural place to fix it now that the variable is properly guarded.)

findings.title: Return statement is redundant and obscures intent
findings.body: Line 70 returns `entryPointAssetsCache, err` after having just assigned `entryPointAssetsCache = result` on line 69. Both expressions yield the same pointer, but reading the code one must verify that no other goroutine could have changed the global between the assignment and the return. While holding the write Lock this is safe, but the redundancy invites future bugs (e.g. someone removing the mutex thinking the local `result` is the returned value). Simply `return result, err` is clearer and removes the indirection.
